task.task_name: Fix round 4: tests that pin the clears and guards of the explorer's error state (round 4's F-001, F-002)
task.description:
Two minor findings of review round 4 on the tests of fix round 3 (task T24). The code is correct today; both findings ask for tests that pin it, so no production file changes in this task. Each finding is in `fix_context.review_feedback` with its file and the reviewer's suggested fix; the full text and the evidence are in findings.json, and every mutant (file:line, anchor, replacement, killed or survived) in research-evidence/mutation-2.md and mutants-r4.json. The task is done when every finish line below holds, MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx and the type check pass, and nothing outside that test file changed.

F-001. The explorer's error state is `{ source: "catalog" | "rebuild", message } | null`. A read the user starts (Retry on the banner, Refresh catalog, the reload after a rebuild) clears it at its start, in the catalog effect's body, and a rebuild clears it at its start, in `rebuild()`; neither clear reads `source`. The tests pin both clears only for a standing catalog-read error, so R4-10 (the effect body's clear keeps a rebuild error) and R4-11 (the clear in `rebuild()` keeps a rebuild error) survive. Finish line: with `onRebuild` rejecting, the rebuild's failure banner shows; then a read the user starts whose catalog read succeeds leaves no banner; and, in its own case, a second Rebuild graph held pending shows no banner while it runs. `scratch_check4.py mutants --ids R4-10,R4-11 --tests src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx` reports both killed.

F-002. Two guards of the catalog effect are unpinned: the clear a quiet read makes on success sits after the check that drops a superseded read (`if (generation !== catalogRead.current) return;`), and the failure write is guarded by `generation === catalogRead.current`. R4-8 (the clear moved above that check, so a superseded quiet read that lands late removes a newer read's failure banner) and R4-7 (the guard dropped, so a superseded read's late failure writes a banner above a newer catalog) survive. Finish line: tests with a held read, for example (a) a quiet re-read held in flight, then a read the user starts that fails and shows its banner, then the quiet read released as a success: the banner stays; (b) a read the user started held in flight, a later read the user starts that succeeds, then the first one rejects: no banner. `scratch_check4.py mutants --ids R4-7,R4-8 --tests src/metaproject/MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx` reports both killed. If a case cannot be reached through what a user can do (for example, if a read the user starts cannot begin while a quiet read is in flight), say so with the line that prevents it, and pin what can be reached instead.

R4-1, R4-6 and R4-12 also survive and are not in this task: R4-1 and R4-12 were judged equivalent and R4-6 is a guard older than this branch's fixes. In `notes`, give the exact title of every test you add and the mutant ids each one kills, so that the flow's record can cite them. A test added here asserts what a user or a caller can observe: rendered text, roles, the requests the explorer sends, a callback's arguments. If a finish line can be met only by changing production code, do not change it: stop, and say so in `behavior_changes` with `needs_operator: true` and the test that shows it. This is the flow's fourth fix round; `fix_context.iteration` says 3 because the request schema caps it there.

Scope freeze: fix the findings named here and nothing else. Anything else you notice goes into `noticed_not_touched`; a choice the plan's state x event matrix does not decide goes into `behavior_changes` with `needs_operator: true` and its alternatives. A reviewer's `suggested_fix` is a hypothesis: reproduce the finding first, check the suggestion against the matrix, and say in `notes` where your fix diverged from it or where a finding did not reproduce. Existing tests are not weakened or deleted to make room for a fix. The fixes you are correcting were themselves reviewed as answers to findings, and the defects they brought were missed for that reason: for each change you make, name in `notes` who else reads the thing you changed (search for it) and what they now get.

review_feedback.message: The clear a read the user starts makes at its start (the effect body, line 380) and the clear a rebuild makes at its start (rebuild(), line 677) are pinned for a standing catalog-source error only. Run in a scratch copy of apps/desktop at 744d9ef75 against MetaprojectView.dom.test.tsx (baseline exit 0, 87 pass): R4-10 (the effect body's `setError(null);` -> `setError(current => current?.source === "rebuild" ? current : null);`, so a loud read keeps a failed rebuild's banner) SURVIVED (exit 0); R4-11 (rebuild()'s `setError(null);` -> the same functional form, so a second rebuild keeps the first one's failure message) SURVIVED (exit 0). Killed for contrast: T24-8 and T24-9 (the clears removed altogether), R4-4, R4-9. T24.result.json's table has the cells 'failed rebuild x loud read started after it, or a new rebuild: cleared at start, as before' and cites 'after a quiet re-read on return, a rebuild's failed catalog reload is still shown'; that test makes a catalog read fail after a rebuild and never starts a read or a rebuild while a rebuild's failure stands. No test builds `source: "rebuild"` followed by Retry, Refresh catalog, or a second Rebuild graph.
review_feedback.suggested_fix: One test: onRebuild throws, banner shows the rebuild message; click Retry on the banner (read succeeds) and expect no banner; repeat with a second Rebuild graph click held pending and expect no banner while 'Rebuilding…' shows. Kills R4-10 and R4-11.

review_feedback.message: The order of the new clear against the 'superseded read' check and the latest-read guard of the failure write are unpinned. R4-8 (the clear moved above `if (generation !== catalogRead.current) return;`, so a quiet read that a later read has superseded still clears a catalog banner when it lands) SURVIVED (exit 0). R4-7 (`if (generation === catalogRead.current && !quiet) setError(` -> `if (!quiet) setError(`, so a superseded read's late failure writes the banner) SURVIVED (exit 0). R4-2 (clear only in the changed-snapshot branch), R4-3 (only in the unchanged one) and R4-4 killed. No fixture holds a catalog read in flight, starts a later read, and lets the first land.
review_feedback.suggested_fix: Two tests with a held read: (a) held quiet read, then a failing Rebuild reload, then release the quiet read as a success: the rebuild-reload banner stays; (b) held loud read, a later read that succeeds, then the first rejects: no banner. Kills R4-8 and R4-7.
